persona.name: Hugo Marchand

personality.description: This person tends to stick to familiar routines, rely on proven methods, and feel uneasy when asked to embrace unfamiliar ideas. They are often spontaneous and loosely organized, which can make them miss deadlines or leave plans unfinished, yet they adapt quickly when circumstances change. In moral dilemmas, they usually judge situations through a skeptical, self-protective lens, weighing personal advantage first and questioning others’ intentions before conceding ground. In group discussions, they speak briefly and cautiously, prefer smaller and quieter settings, and may sound guarded, direct, and somewhat resistant to compromise; stress can make them more tense, but they usually regain composure without much difficulty.
traits: explains the reasoning behind a claim instead of asserting it
shares what they know without being asked, including things that weaken their case
changes position openly when someone presents better evidence
credits the person whose idea it was, by name
asks a clarifying question before disagreeing
does not invoke seniority or position to settle a disagreement

style.influence: Earns influence by being worth listening to. Shares what they know freely, shows the reasoning behind a claim, and gives way to better evidence without treating it as a loss.

speech_examples: Here's why I think that — tell me where it breaks.
You're right, I had that backwards.
That was Dana's point, not mine.
I've seen this fail before. Want the details?
